title: Push Notification System
vague_prompt: Design a push notification system that sends millions of messages.
hidden_guidance: 200 million notifications per day, with a peak of 20 thousand per second
Channels are mobile push through APNs and FCM, email, and SMS
Delivery to the provider must start within 5 seconds of the event at p95
Each user has per channel and per category preferences plus quiet hours
A failed send retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff, then goes to a dead letter queue
The same event must not notify one user twice inside a 24 hour window
known_patterns: Event intake queue in front of the fanout service
Fanout service that checks user preferences before it sends
One queue per channel with a provider adapter for each
Retry with exponential backoff and a dead letter queue
Dedup by event id and user id
Delivery tracking and provider rate limits
common_misses: Quiet hours computed in the user timezone
Provider rate limits and expired device tokens
Backpressure when one provider is slow
Bounce and unsubscribe handling for email

interviewer_brief.gist: A delivery pipeline that fans one event out to phones, inboxes, and SMS gateways, with a per-person rulebook. About 2,315 notifications per second on average and 20 thousand at peak, and the guarantees are timing, preferences, and never the same notification twice.

1: About 200 million notifications per day, about 2,315 per second on average with a peak of 20 thousand per second
Channels: mobile push through APNs and FCM, plus email and SMS
Dispatch to the provider starts within 5 seconds of the event at p95
A strong candidate asks for volume, channel mix, and the dispatch budget instead of inventing them.
2: An event bus receives triggers; a fan-out layer resolves audience and channels; provider adapters send
Each channel has its own adapter and rate limits: APNs, FCM, email, SMS
Sketch the path: event, dedupe, preference check, channel queue, provider
A strong candidate keeps channel specifics inside adapters.
3: The 5 second budget makes the event to dispatch path short: a queue, a preference lookup, a provider call
Preferences and quiet hours are one keyed lookup per user, cached
Bulk campaigns and single events share the path but ride separate queues so a campaign cannot delay a single event
A strong candidate isolates campaign bursts from single events.
4: Provider rate limits are the bottleneck, not the internal bus: 20 thousand per second must spread across provider quotas
Retries up to 5 with exponential backoff stretch delivery over about 31 seconds before a dead letter queue
The dedupe window: one event never notifies one user twice inside 24 hours, keyed by user plus event
A strong candidate treats provider quotas as capacity and the dedupe key as a correctness feature.
5: Per channel and per category preferences plus quiet hours gate every send
The dead letter queue captures exhausted sends for inspection and replay
Delivery receipts and provider feedback close the loop per notification
A strong candidate makes preferences enforceable at dispatch time, not just at compose time.

anchors.1: Hearing the volume: the candidate states about 200 million per day with a 20 thousand per second peak
anchors.2: Hearing the channels: the candidate names mobile push through APNs and FCM, email, and SMS
anchors.3: Hearing the budget: the candidate dispatches to providers within 5 seconds at p95
anchors.4: Hearing the rulebook: the candidate applies per channel and per category preferences with quiet hours
anchors.5: Hearing the retry: the candidate retries up to 5 times with backoff, then dead letters
anchors.6: Hearing the dedupe: the candidate blocks repeat notifications for one user and one event inside 24 hours

probes.q: A campaign targets 80 million users at noon. What does your peak look like, and what absorbs it?
One event must reach a user's phone, inbox, and SMS. Walk me through what happens and where it can fan out.
Dispatch must start within 5 seconds. What sits between the event and the provider call?
It is 2 AM for the user and a marketing event fires. Who decides that nothing is sent, and when?
FCM rejects a batch because of a rate limit. What happens to those notifications over the next minute?
A payment event retried and the user got two alerts. What key would have stopped that?
